Commentary.Commentary: Not surprisingly, JOS BUTTLER has been named the Man Of The Match. What next for Australia? Another ODI series gone. Playing for pride remains, with 2 games left. Can they avert a whitewash? Chance 1 will come on Australia Day, 26th January, 2018 in the fourth ODI at the Adelaide Oval, at 1350 local (0320 GMT). Do join us then. In the meanwhile, you can check how Sri Lanka is faring against Zimbabwe in their must-win game. ADIOS! Take Care!

How to respond when one of your mates goes down? South Africa showed that twice in a Test - once against Australia and once against India recently when Dale Steyn was out injured. Tonight, England have done it in the absence of Liam Plunkett. They  would have been worried with the loss of a bowler but the team combined together well as a unit. Only Joe Root went for runs tonight while the others did really well to share the spoils.

Steven Smith edged one behind and after numerous replays, was adjudged caught behind. From some angles it seemed like the ball had bounced. After that, the Aussies started to lose their grip on the game. There was a 74-run stand between Marcus Stoinis and Tim Paine towards the end but the required rate was always getting tougher.

Australia actually batted well on a sluggish surface with a lot of intent. David Warner and Cameron White departed early but the 69-run stand between Aaron Finch and Steven Smith got things under track. Finch departed but then the skipper got a handy partnership with junior Marsh. And then, came the controversial moment.

A really good win for England, in fact their best of the series. Even though the margin is only 16 runs. It is because they were struggling with the bat around the 40th over and then they were a bowler short. Add to this, Australia were ahead of them throughout the run chase till the 50th over. Kudos to such a performance.

A short ball on middle, pulled through mid-wicket for another single. The game ends. Sam Billings collects and then roars towards the crowd. England's first bilateral series win in ODIs in Australia! 3-0 up with 2 to go!

OUT! The umpire's call stays! Is that the game? Wood is running around in frenzy. Outside off, on a length, Smith flashes hard and gets a thick outside edge. It is referred upstairs with the soft signal as out and after numerous replays, eventually, the third umpire declares it as OUT. Now, whether he felt that it carried or was he not sure, hence went with the onfield call, one never knows. But Smith has to go.
Is that out? Smith has nicked one to Buttler but the umpires want to check whether it carried. The soft signal is OUT.

OUT! Umpire's call and Finch has to walk back! A huge, huge wicket! Aaron Finch's magical stay comes to an end. Rashid tosses it on leg stump, and it straightens. Finch goes for the sweep shot which he has played ever so well but this time he misses to get hit on the pads. The English players appeal, Rashid is actually pleading there. After a long though, the umpire raises his finger. Finch immediately reviews and why not he is Australia's in form batsman. They go upstairs and replays show there is no inside edge. Hawk Eye shows it is clipping leg. The on-field call stays and a timely wicket for England. Finch walks back after a very good half century but the home sided needed more from him. The 69-run stand has been broken and the away side will now look to take command of the game. The hosts are 200 away.

Cameron White walks out at no. 3. A promotion for him.

OUT! Woakes draws first blood! Warner bags another failure. Woakes bowls the slower ball, an off cutter outside off. Warner tries to punch it through the off side but is done in by the slowness off the wicket. He hits it uppishly to Hales at cover-point who takes one of the easiest catches he will ever get. Good change of pace by Woakes. He did it with the bat first and now gives England an early wicket and also a big one. They are ecstatic and now they would look to put a lid on the scoring.
Good length outside off, Finch guides it down to third man for a run.
Another ball outside off, Finch tries to guide but does not connect.
FOUR! Australians are off to a flier here! Finch gets a short ball on his hips. Not where you should be bowling with fine leg up. He pulls it through that region and a boundary result.
On a length around off, defended.

Superb fielding! On a length around off, Finch pushes it on the up, through cover-point. There are two fielders giving it a chase. One from point and one from cover-point. Morgan is the one to get it it as he dives and pulls it back. Roy picks it up and fires a throw to the keeper. Three taken.
On a length around off, stays low a touch. Finch defends it off the toe end. He wants a run but there was never one there.
Well bowled and well played! Good cricket all around there. Wood bowls a yorker on off, Finch jams it out to mid off.
Length ball on off, defended towards mid on.
FOUR LEG BYES! Poor ball! Wood sprays it on the pads, Finch tries to flick but misses, the ball brushes off the pads and goes down to fine leg for a boundary.
Hits the length hard on off, Finch defends it back towards mid on.
A good ball to finish the over! A length ball on middle, Warner defends it back towards the bowler.
Back of a length on off, guided to point.
Full and wide outside off, drives it towards covers. The fielder there makes a good stop diving to his left.

FOUR! Short and put away! A bumper on middle, Warner swivels inside the crease and pulls it through square leg for a boundary. Attacking start by the Australian openers, they have to make most of the new ball as scoring is going to get difficult.
Nice shot! Shorter in length around off, Finch pushes it through covers for three. Not sure it will be easy to play these shots once the ball gets a little old.
On a length around off, it jags back in a touch. Finch is beaten as he tries to flick. It hits him high on the pads, the English players make a mute appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Chris Woakes who was outstanding with the bat will bowl with the second new ball.
A dot to finish! A length ball on off, Warner keeps it out.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! Wood bowls it a touch fuller on off, Warner loves it there, he leans into it and drives it through covers and the ball races away.
Back of a length on off, defended.
Good length outside off, Warner lets it be.

PEACH! Wood lands it on a length around off, gets good bounce on that one. Almost similar to the delivery he got Warner out in the first game. This time though, Warner hangs his bat out only to get beaten.
Back of a length on off, punched through point for a single, to get underway.
The players are back out in the middle already! Was that even a break? Anyways, here is Mark Wood to Aaron Finch first up. David Warner is at the other end...
